text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone is not evidence. All-female panels occur routinely by chance and in fields where women are well represented in HR and compliance; if you'd been hired by that same panel, you wouldn't read anything into it. Raising it makes you look like you're reverse-engineering a grievance from a photograph, and it undermines the stronger point you actually have.

That stronger point is the unanswered request. Chase it in writing, cite any statutory deadline, and ask for the scoring criteria, weightings and your scores against the appointee's. If the criteria were drafted after shortlisting, or "regulatory affairs" was never in the advertised spec, that's substantive. Qualifications gaps alone don't prove bias — panels can legitimately prefer regulatory fluency over modelling depth.
